title: QQ plot

blocks.what_we_do:
Draw a QQ plot. It compares the p-values we observed with the p-values we would expect if no variant were linked to the disease. We use only the [autosomal](docs/glossary.md#autosome) variants, on chromosomes 1 to 22.

The plot reads the [summary statistics file](docs/glossary.md#summary-statistics) that we made at step 6.8. This file is a table with one row for each tested variant. Each row holds the chromosome, the position, the alleles, the odds ratio, the standard error, the p-value and the number of samples. The plots in this module all read this one file, so every figure comes from the same results.
blocks.why:
A [QQ plot](docs/glossary.md#qq-plot) puts the observed p-values in order and pairs each one with the value that we expect by chance. If no variant is linked to the disease, the [p-values](docs/glossary.md#p-value) are spread evenly between 0 and 1. The plot shows -log10 of each p-value. This turns small p-values into large positive numbers, so strong results appear high on the plot.

If the tests behave well, the points follow the diagonal line. A few strong associations lift only the highest points at the right end. A wider departure along the whole line can have several causes: [confounding](docs/glossary.md#confounding), technical problems, a wrong model or many true small effects. The picture alone cannot tell these causes apart. Nearby variants can be correlated through [linkage disequilibrium (LD)](docs/glossary.md#ld), so the points are not fully independent.
blocks.you_need: The summary statistics file from step 6.8. If R says that the file is missing, run step 6.8 first.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-1}
stats <- guided_summary_stats(cfg)
autosomal <- stats$chromosome %in% as.character(1:22)
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.1", "qq.png"), function() plot_qq(stats$p_value[autosomal], "Adjusted simulated GWAS: autosomal QQ plot"))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R chunk is the complete command.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
Most points are close to the diagonal line. The highest points at the right end leave the line strongly. Missing, zero or invalid p-values are not drawn as if they were strong results. R saves the picture as a PNG file and prints its path. It does not show the picture in the console. To see it, open the file from the Files pane of RStudio (click the file name, then choose "View File").

The tested PLINK version is set in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: the executable chunks, the comparisons with the expected results and the final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file that R names and the previous step. Keep the command and the messages from the console. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does a strong departure only at the highest points always mean confounding across the whole genome?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. A few true signals can lift the highest points while most other tests stay close to the line.

</details>

figures.gemini_prompt: Draw a teaching QQ schematic showing a diagonal null distribution, a tail-only departure and broad inflation in separate labelled panels. Explain possible causes without labelling every departure confounding; use line styles and text as well as colour.
figures.alt_text: Most adjusted autosomal tests follow the null diagonal, with an upper-tail departure from a few association signals.
